body:
A vape kit bundles everything needed to start: a battery device, a tank or pod and usually a charging cable. If you are an adult trying vaping for the first time, or moving on from a disposable, a kit is often better value than buying parts separately, and it avoids compatibility mistakes. But kits differ a lot, and a first purchase can go wrong if you pick the wrong type or the wrong liquid. This guide explains what comes in the box, how to choose between pod kits and tank kits, which features matter, how to pick a liquid, how to set up and use a kit, how to avoid common beginner mistakes, what to buy as extras and how to look after it. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## What comes in the box
Most starter kits include the device, one or two pods or a tank, a replacement coil and a USB cable. Some include a lanyard or case. Liquid is normally sold separately. Check the listing for what is included, and for the pod type and coil resistance. Our catalog lists more than 250 kits, from compact pod devices to larger systems. See [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/).

## Pod kit or tank kit
Pod kits are the simplest. You fill or swap a pod and press to draw or use a button. Tank kits add adjustable airflow and more power. For beginners, a pod kit is easier. Browse our [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/) and read [disposable vs pod vs box mod](/blog/disposable-vs-pod-vs-box-mod/) to decide. If you are moving on from a disposable, a pod kit feels familiar, with a small body and a simple draw.

### Closed pod kits
These use pre-filled pods that you replace when empty. They are convenient and leak-resistant, but you are limited to the flavors made for that device.

### Open pod kits
These use refillable pods. You choose your own liquid, which gives more flavors and lower running costs, at the price of a little effort.

### Tank kits
These use a larger tank and coils. They suit people who want more vapor and adjustment, and they need more care.

## Features that matter
- **Battery size:** measured in mAh. Larger lasts longer, but is bulkier. See [mAh, puffs and battery life](/blog/mah-puffs-and-battery-life-how-they-relate/).
- **Charging:** USB-C is faster and easier to replace than older ports.
- **Draw style:** auto-draw devices fire when you inhale; button devices fire when pressed. See [auto-draw vs button-fire vapes](/blog/auto-draw-vs-button-fire-vapes/).
- **Pod capacity:** bigger pods mean fewer refills.
- **Coil type:** mesh coils give smooth flavor. See [what is a mesh coil](/blog/what-is-a-mesh-coil/).
- **Airflow:** adjustable airflow lets you tune the draw. See [adjustable airflow explained](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/).

## Picking a liquid
Match nicotine type to the device. Pods generally pair with nicotine salts, so look at [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) labeled for pods. Our guide to [salts versus freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/) explains the difference. Choose a PG/VG ratio of about 50/50 for pods; see [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/). Start with a 30 mL bottle, which lasts a while, and a flavor you know you like. See [e-liquid bottle sizes](/blog/e-liquid-bottle-sizes-30ml-60ml-100ml/) and [how to read an e-liquid label](/blog/how-to-read-an-e-liquid-label/).

## Setting up your first kit
1. Charge the device fully before the first use.
2. Unpack the pod or tank, and check the coil is fitted.
3. Prime the coil: add a few drops of liquid to the cotton, if exposed.
4. Fill the pod or tank below the max line, without overfilling.
5. Seat the pod firmly until it clicks.
6. Let it rest for five to ten minutes, so that the coil soaks.
7. Take a few gentle puffs, then use as normal.

Read [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/) before the first use, because it prevents the most common beginner problem.

## Common beginner mistakes
- **Overfilling a pod,** which causes leaks.
- **Not priming a new coil,** which can burn it.
- **Using the wrong liquid thickness,** such as thick high-VG liquid in a small pod.
- **Choosing a nicotine strength that is too high.** See [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/).
- **Chain vaping,** which dries the wick.
- **Ignoring battery care.**

## A worked example
You choose a pod kit with a 1,000 mAh battery, a USB-C port, auto-draw and a refillable 2 mL pod, priced at about $25. You buy a 30 mL bottle of nicotine salt liquid at 35 mg/mL in a fruit flavor, for about $12. You charge the device, prime the coil, fill the pod to the line, wait ten minutes and start. A bottle lasts several weeks, and a pod lasts a week or two. After a month, you buy a spare pod and another flavor. Your running cost is a fraction of what you would pay for disposables, and you can change flavors as you like.

## What to buy as extras
A spare pod or coil, so that a worn one can be swapped at once; a small case, to protect the device; a second flavor, to rotate; and a good USB-C cable. Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) for spares that match your device. Check the exact model before you order, because parts are not interchangeable between brands.

## Looking after your kit
Keep it clean and dry, charge it with a suitable charger, store it upright and replace pods and coils when flavor fades. See [how to clean a vape device](/blog/how-to-clean-a-vape-device/), [how to extend vape battery life](/blog/how-to-extend-vape-battery-life/) and [battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/). Keep liquids and devices out of reach of children and pets.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Do I need to buy liquid separately?
Usually yes, unless the kit includes pre-filled pods. Check the listing.

### Can I use any liquid in my kit?
No. Match nicotine type and PG/VG ratio to the device. Pods generally pair with salts.

### How long will a kit last?
The battery lasts months with care, pods and coils last weeks, and you will replace parts regularly.

### Is a kit cheaper than disposables?
Often over time, depending on your use. Compare per month.

### What if my kit does not work?
See [why a vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/) and [what to do when a vape will not charge](/blog/vape-wont-charge-fixes/), and contact us if it is faulty from new.

## Shop
Browse [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A buying checklist for your first kit
1. Decide pod kit or tank kit, and choose a pod kit if unsure.
2. Check the battery size and USB-C charging.
3. Check what is in the box and what is not.
4. Check that spare pods and coils are easy to find.
5. Choose a liquid that suits the device, and a strength you are comfortable with.
6. Plan a spare pod or coil, and a case.
7. Check the seller's policies and delivery.

## A worked first-month budget
Suppose the kit costs $25, a 30 mL bottle of liquid $12, a pack of spare pods or coils $8 and a case $6, so $51 up front. In the first month you use the liquid, one or two coils and the battery. In month two you may need another bottle and a pack of coils, about $20. Compare that with disposables at about $18 each, where you might use two in a month, about $36. Over several months, the kit becomes cheaper, but only if you keep using it. If you stop, you will have spent more than you would have on a single disposable, so be honest with yourself.

## What to do if you do not like it
Opened or used products cannot be returned under our policy, so think before you buy. If you are unsure, try a disposable first, or ask us for advice with your usual habits and budget. See [refund and return policy explained](/blog/refund-and-return-policy-explained/).

## Good habits from the first day
Charge the device when it is low, not flat. Fill pods carefully. Prime new coils. Replace pods and coils on time. Store the device upright, in a cool place. Keep liquid and devices away from children and pets. These habits take no effort, and they prevent most problems.

## Frequently asked questions about first kits
### Can I use my kit while it charges?
Only if the manual says so. It is better to wait until charging is finished.

### How do I know when to change the pod?
When flavor fades, the vapor thins or a burnt taste appears, or when the pod looks dirty. Do not wait until it is dry.

### Should I buy a spare kit?
A spare pod or coil is more useful than a spare kit. If you rely on your device, a backup disposable is handy.

### What if the pod leaks?
Check that it is seated properly and not overfilled, and wipe the device. See [leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/).

### How do I clean the kit?
Wipe the outside and the contacts with a dry cloth or cotton bud. Do not wet the battery. See [how to clean a vape device](/blog/how-to-clean-a-vape-device/).

### Where do I find help?
Ask us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your device name and what is happening.
